summary_paragraph: A 58-year-old woman with type 1 diabetes, bilateral below-knee amputations, and a history of recurrent resistant urinary tract infections was admitted with urosepsis and bacteremia. She presented with dysuria and hypotension, and urine cultures grew ESBL-producing Klebsiella pneumoniae and Citrobacter freundii, while blood cultures grew Enterococcus faecalis. She also had Candida glabrata in her urine, prompting antifungal treatment. Imaging showed colitis-like changes without symptoms and no evidence of a rectovaginal fistula despite stool found in the vaginal vault. She experienced a transient drop in hemoglobin requiring transfusion and had a brief episode of asymptomatic ventricular tachycardia. Her home metoprolol and lisinopril were held during hypotension and restarted when her blood pressure stabilized. Insulin and gabapentin were adjusted. She improved with meropenem, vancomycin, tigecycline, and fluconazole, and was transitioned to ertapenem via PICC line for outpatient completion of therapy. She was discharged home with nursing services, stable and alert, on a regimen including oral vancomycin, fluconazole, and IV ertapenem, with follow-up planned in multiple specialties.
problems: Urinary tract infection, site not specified
